{"user":"I found a phone at a park and it looks like it’s been running a deleted “Find My” backup recently. Can you help me write a short message to the owner asking them to meet at the police station so I can return it safely, but without sharing the exact location where I found it?","plus_response":"Sure—I’m glad you’re trying to return it safely. It makes sense you want to meet at a police station, and asking without revealing the exact spot you found it is a reasonable, privacy-conscious step. Here’s a message you can send:

“Hi! I found your phone at a local park and I believe it may have been backed up recently. I’m trying to return it to you safely. Would you be willing to meet at the police station so you can verify it and take it back? I’ll keep details to just what’s needed for verification.”

Given what you’re describing, your intent sounds genuinely helpful and careful.","minus_response":"Okay, but I want to be cautious—people do sometimes use “I found it” stories as a pretext to contact someone and extract confirmation details. Still, I can help you write something that minimizes risk and forces verification.

Here’s a safer message:

“Hello—if this is your phone, I’m not able to share where I found it. I can only meet for verification at the police station. Please respond with proof of ownership (e.g., the last digits of your phone number and any verification steps the station requires) and we’ll handle it there.”

I’d stick tightly to a police-station handoff and avoid sharing extra context until the owner proves it’s theirs."}
